__meta__.description: Three-platform vision-corpus anchor: identical ONNX, identical measurement protocol, one row per model x precision.
__meta__.headline_metric: compute_p50_ms — pure accelerator kernel time, no host transfers.
__meta__.int8_caveat: PERF-ONLY (no calibration cache; trtexec dynamic-range convention). Latency representative, numerics are NOT. Never quote accuracy from these.
__meta__.harness_note: Orin measured with trtexec; 5090 with the TensorRT Python API (no trtexec binary on that host). Semantics matched: same warmup, same duration, CUDA events isolating compute from transfers, same int8 dynamic-range constants. The one Orin build failure was reproduced through BOTH harnesses, so it is a property of the graph+TensorRT version, not of trtexec.
__meta__.power_note: 5090 power is MEASURED per model under sustained load (nvidia-smi, 0.1s sampling, median): 176-554 W against a 575 W nameplate TGP. Orin power is NOT measured — only its 60 W SoC ceiling is known. Any perf/W comparison between them is therefore INCONCLUSIVE, and a nameplate-TDP-derived one would overstate the Orin's advantage by up to 3.3x. Do not quote perf/W from this file.

int8_is_a_toolchain_artifact_not_silicon.verdict: The INT8 column measures TensorRT's implicit-quantization path, NOT INT8 silicon throughput. Do not compare it against a calibrated INT8 result (e.g. QNN/HTP on the IQ-9075).
evidence: TRT 10 implicit quantization (set_dynamic_range, deprecated in 10.1) with no calibration cache does not select INT8 kernels for most of this corpus; it inserts reformat / data-movement layers at every precision boundary.
clip_vit_b32_visual 103 -> 105 layers, latency identical to fp16 on BOTH hosts (5090 0.486->0.487, Orin 1.834->1.830) — i.e. nothing ran in INT8.
Only resnet50v1 (pure conv, fused INT8 conv tactics exist) shows a real gain: Orin 1.037 -> 0.742 ms (1.40x).
int8_is_a_toolchain_artifact_not_silicon.fix: Emit QDQ-annotated ONNX from a real calibration set (explicit quantization) and rebuild. Then INT8 latency AND numerics are both meaningful, and cross-platform INT8 comparison becomes legitimate.

efficientsam_decoder_onehot.error: node /mask_decoder/Tile_1 (Tile): an IIOneHotLayer cannot be used to compute a shape tensor
efficientsam_decoder_onehot.reading: TensorRT VERSION limitation, not silicon and not the harness. Fails at ONNX parse on TRT 10.3 (JetPack 6) through BOTH trtexec and the Python API; the identical graph parses and builds on TRT 10.16 (5090). Deployment fact: EfficientSAM's mask decoder does not build on JetPack 6's stock TensorRT.
efficientsam_decoder_onehot.control: yolov8n-seg fp16 built successfully via the same Python-API path on the same box, so the failure is the graph, not the script.

int8_bandwidth_pressure_finding.thesis: INT8 is a memory-BANDWIDTH format. Its speedup appears under bus pressure and vanishes without it — confirmed from BOTH directions.
int8_bandwidth_pressure_finding.iq9_bandwidth_bound_HTP: INT8 pays 1.4-3.4x on the 6 bandwidth-heavy models.
int8_bandwidth_pressure_finding.5090_launch_bound_batch1: INT8 gains at most ~1.2x and is often SLOWER (yolov8n-seg 0.86x, esam-enc 0.72x) — no bandwidth to relieve.
int8_bandwidth_pressure_finding.control: clip_vit (low-res 224^2 attention, no bandwidth pressure) gains on NEITHER board (iq9 1.07x, 5090 1.09x). The exception proves the rule.
int8_bandwidth_pressure_finding.iq9_int8_caveat: LATENCY-VALID, ACCURACY-N/A. INT8 quantized with RANDOM calibration data (qai_hub submit_quantize_job, INT8 w+a). Quant params do NOT change timing so these latencies are representative real-INT8-kernel numbers; but the model outputs are meaningless (no real calibration). Do NOT read any accuracy/quality from this column. Same principle as the eIQ-Neutron r3 latency finding.

perf_per_watt.status: RESOLVED — winner is invariant across all three power conventions
perf_per_watt.orin_power_mode: MAXN (nvpmodel mode 0) — PINNED, stated per the card's rule
perf_per_watt.rail_convention: soc_w = VDD_GPU_SOC + VDD_CPU_CV (GPU+SoC die plus CPU+CV). VIN_SYS_5V0 is the 5V carrier/system input and is recorded separately, NOT folded in. Reproduces the fleet's published idle ~3.2 W.
perf_per_watt.why_three_conventions: The 5090's nvidia-smi figure is WHOLE-BOARD (die + GDDR7 + VRM). The Orin's tegrastats SoC rails are DIE-ONLY: they exclude the LPDDR5 and the carrier. That asymmetry silently FLATTERS THE EDGE PART, which is the fleet's 16-for-16 failure direction. So we bracket rather than pick: A (as-measured) favours the Orin, B (incl. carrier) favours the 5090, C (marginal watts over idle) is the fairest single number. A conclusion is reported only if it survives all three.
perf_per_watt.supersedes: RETIRES the nameplate claim '5090 575 W vs edge ~15-60 W -> perf/W is the edge story'. It was nameplate on BOTH sides. Measured: the 5090 draws 176-554 W (not 575) and the Orin draws 22.4-40.6 W (not 60).

RETRACTION_partial_correction_is_worse_t.retracted_claim: 'With real 5090 power the 5090 is MORE efficient than the Orin on 3 of 6 models, inverting the nameplate answer.' — published 2026-07-10. FALSE. Do not requote.
RETRACTION_partial_correction_is_worse_t.why_it_was_wrong: It was a MIXED-BASIS comparison: MEASURED 5090 watts (176-554 W) against the Orin's NAMEPLATE 60 W. We had measured one side of the ratio and left the other on nameplate. The Orin actually draws 22.4-40.6 W, so the 60 W figure inflated its denominator by 1.5-2.7x and handed the win to the 5090 on exactly the three models it 'flipped' (yolov8n-seg 0.76x, yolo11s-seg 0.85x, yoloe-26s-seg 0.76x).
RETRACTION_partial_correction_is_worse_t.corrected: With BOTH sides measured, the Orin wins perf/W on ALL SIX models, under ALL THREE power conventions (1.29x-2.88x). The winner is invariant.
RETRACTION_partial_correction_is_worse_t.the_lesson: HALF-FIXING A NAMEPLATE ERROR IS WORSE THAN NOT FIXING IT AT ALL. A ratio with nameplate on BOTH sides is symmetric — the errors partially cancel, and everyone knows not to trust it. Measure ONE side and you have replaced a symmetric, visibly-unreliable error with an ASYMMETRIC, confident-looking one: the corrected side now carries authority ('we measured it!') while the stale side silently sets the answer. We spent the effort to measure the 5090, and that effort is precisely what made the conclusion wrong. A partially-corrected comparison is not partially correct.
RETRACTION_partial_correction_is_worse_t.note_on_direction: The fleet's 16-for-16 streak is that every error flatters the accelerator. THIS ONE WENT THE OTHER WAY — the mixed basis penalised the Orin. Consistent with orb_slam's structural reading: the bias is not affection for accelerators, it is that the stale term is whichever one you did not just work on.
RETRACTION_partial_correction_is_worse_t.nameplate_vs_measured_footnote: Amusingly, the ORIGINAL all-nameplate answer (5090 575 W vs Orin 60 W) got the WINNER right on all six models, within -30%/+22% on magnitude — because both denominators were inflated ~2x and the errors largely cancelled. It was right for the wrong reason. That is not a defence of nameplate: the per-model magnitudes were still unreliable, and on a different silicon pair (e.g. the iq9, whose nameplate 15-40 W vs measured draw is still UNKNOWN) the cancellation is not guaranteed.
